answer: Weight comes from winning, not from registering. Seats enrolled in the same window are reshuffled into a cohort each round by a sealed beacon, and each pair argues one question before a panel of uninvolved peers; credit is paid only for a crystal clear verdict, a decisive margin the panel can defend publicly. Mirrored briefs and near-ties pay nothing, so a batch of clones mostly fights itself for one credit, internal pairings growing with the square of the batch across the horizon. Each clone still posts a stake, and per-seat yield sinks to its nadir.
